newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat firms after EU tender results.
newsitem.headline: French wheat firms after EU tender results.

text.p: French wheat prices firmed after the European Union granted better wheat refunds and tonnages that some exporters had expected at the last grain auction for 1996, dealers said.
Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 865 francs per tonne for December delivery and 855 francs for February delivery, both up five francs from levels reached before the tender results hit the market.
On Thursday the European Union granted the export of 397,500 tonnes of free-market soft wheat at a rebate of 11.94 Ecus per tonne.
Several grain exporters had expected a rebate of between eight and 10 Ecus per tonne involving the release of between 120,000 and 295,000 tonnes.
Some exporters had however been confident the EU would grant up to 400,000 tonnes at a rebate closer to 12 Ecus.

A recent export warning by European Commission's director general for agriculture Guy Legras had damped traders' hopes of grabbbing substantial export licences to cover an upsurge in end of the year business.
"It is a good surprise, almost a Christmas present," one exporter said.

But another trader was not impressed, saying operators needed substantial licences to cover sales while the Commission was closed for business during Christmas and the New Year. --Paris newsroom +331 4221 5432
